title: Food transformation process
supported_claim: FoodOn represents transformation processes with inputs and outputs; processes add or remove qualities; ordered process applications must not be collapsed into contradictory parallel assertions.
limitation: FoodOn concerns human and domesticated-animal food broadly and does not prescribe ERA property names or classify every AOM feed process.

title: FoodOn structure
supported_claim: FoodOn places transformation processes under process and explicitly states that processes may be multi-purpose or tied to different process objectives.
limitation: FoodOn acknowledges purpose variation but its public hierarchy does not provide ERA's proposed four-layer relation model directly.

title: FoodOn Robot Process source table
supported_claim: FoodOn distinguishes component separation, physical or chemical modification, microbial or enzymatic modification, forming, preservation, fat removal, water removal, component addition, fermentation, extraction, hydrolysis, distillation, and rendering; many processes have multiple parents.
limitation: Editorial source includes LanguaL imports and some classification-only groupings; it mixes mechanism, operation, objective, and preservation in one class hierarchy and should guide vocabulary comparison rather than be copied wholesale.

title: Consolidated Regulation (EU) No 68/2013 Part B glossary of processes
supported_claim: Feed-specific process definitions distinguish direct operations and results including size reduction, component removal, concentration, detoxification, distillation, drying, ensiling, extraction, fermentation, grinding, hydrolysis, pressing, and soaking.
limitation: Regulatory catalogue supports naming and process scope in EU feed commerce; definitions often combine mechanism and objective and do not establish universal nutritional benefit.

title: Core classes
supported_claim: OBI separates planned process, plan specification, material inputs and outputs, and resulting data, supporting separation of process type, intention, execution, and measured outcome.
limitation: OBI is investigation-focused rather than feed-processing authority and is used only as modelling precedent.

title: Poultry by-product meal
supported_claim: Poultry by-product meal production can include stabilization, rendering, cooking or sterilization, drying, fat extraction, and grinding; rendering is a multi-stage process rather than a synonym for one objective.
limitation: Evidence supports poultry by-product meal and related rendering practice; it cannot establish every rendering route or output globally.

title: Manure and poultry litter
supported_claim: Deep stacking appears in poultry-litter treatment context and is associated with material-specific aflatoxin reduction; drying, ensiling, heating, and grinding are separately described.
limitation: Datasheet is pending revision and cites older evidence; it does not define deep stacking as one general mechanism or universal feed treatment.

title: AOM Livestock staging graph
supported_claim: Provides current process labels, statuses, parent relations, complete descendant closure, and direct-child counts.
limitation: Current generated graph is review subject and existing placement is not acceptance evidence.

title: Release feed-material facet bindings
supported_claim: Provides every current material-to-processingMethod assertion and concept usage count used to assess migration impact.
limitation: Bindings record governed current semantics but do not independently prove process mechanism, purpose, or benefit.

title: Livestock identifier registry and implementation register
supported_claim: Records Brewhouse processing as retired before publication because it is upstream production provenance rather than feed treatment.
limitation: Decision is local precedent and does not automatically classify unrelated workflows.

title: ADR 0042 Feed-process hierarchy and material-state axes
supported_claim: Establishes one canonical feed-process root, initial mechanism and objective polyhierarchy, separate material-state axes, and non-universal process-result relations.
limitation: Initial objective structure remains incomplete and is superseded where ADR 0047 makes a more precise distinction.

title: ADR 0044 Feed taxonomy axis reclassification
supported_claim: Separates material identity, product role, component, process, composition, and provenance; retires Brewhouse processing from feed-treatment use and retains component separation as objective grouping.
limitation: ADR 0044 did not complete full process-purpose, benefit, or observed-effect modelling.
